checks: APEC explains that a passport-linked business travel card can serve as entry authority for qualifying short business visits to an economy that granted the holder preclearance.
Fully participating APEC economies; qualifying passport-linked card and destination-specific business preclearance
Check the card's clearances, passport and eligibility, each destination's terms, port and permitted stay. Tourism and transit depend on the economy and use case.

Canada and the United States are transitional business travel card participants. APEC describes fast-track processing at participating airports while separate immigration documentation requirements still apply.
Canada and United States; covered APEC Business Travel Card processing
Verify the airport, carrier and itinerary and the traveler's ordinary passport, visa or authorization requirements.

The Andean Community confirms that covered citizens of Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador and Peru can make intracommunity tourism trips with their recognized national identity document, without a passport or visa under the scheme.
Andean Community tourism between its four members for eligible nationals
General Secretariat of the Andean Community
Check acceptable documents for the specific nationality, minors, route, nonmember transit and any entry documentation required for another purpose.
The Andean Community describes international roaming without added surcharges on covered postpaid plans when its members' citizens travel within the community.
Covered postpaid terrestrial mobile plans within Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador and Peru
General Secretariat of the Andean Community
Check operator and plan eligibility, data or reasonable-use conditions and radio, SIM and satellite rules separately.
CARICOM confirms enhanced free movement for qualifying nationals traveling between the four participants, with admission safeguards. Its 2026 review reports implementation in all four.
Barbados, Belize, Dominica and Saint Vincent and the Grenadines; qualifying nationals across the four
Verify passport evidence, family-member eligibility, port procedure, exclusions and national implementation. Other CARICOM nationals may be subject to a different regime.

Under enhanced free movement, eligible nationals of the four participating countries can work in another participating country without the standard work permit or CSME skills certificate described in the CARICOM guidance.
Barbados, Belize, Dominica and Saint Vincent and the Grenadines; participating nationals and employment scope
Verify professional licensing and any regulated activity separately. Entry or removal safeguards still apply.

Article 5 of the ECOWAS free-movement protocol provides for covered private vehicles registered in a member state to enter another member state for up to 90 days with a valid licence, registration, recognized insurance and recognized customs carnet.
ECOWAS treaty framework; inter-member temporary entry with a member-registered private vehicle
Verify actual implementation, precise documents accepted at the crossings, transit, driver qualification, temporary admission and later bilateral arrangements. Commercial routes differ.
Article 3 of the ECOWAS free-movement protocol calls for an international health certificate along with a valid travel document for citizens entering another member state.
ECOWAS treaty framework; covered community citizens on inter-member routes

Verify present-day national implementation and the required certificate, itinerary, vaccines, age rules and exceptions. The protocol alone does not identify an applicable vaccine or certificate for an individual trip.

The ECOWAS Commission's withdrawal communication asked remaining member authorities to keep recognizing certain travel documents and visa-free movement for Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger citizens until further notice.
Remaining ECOWAS member destinations; 2025 transition communication with no definitive end in the cited notice
Search for later implementation decisions and route- or citizenship-specific changes. This notice alone does not establish current local practice or reciprocal admission into former member countries.
The GCC customs guide provides a common framework for passenger effects and gifts, subject to restrictions in applicable common and national lists and to eligibility for relief.
First points of entry within covered Gulf Cooperation Council customs procedures
The regional guide is historical. Seek current destination-level thresholds, traveler exemptions, inspection, and commodity rules before presenting any operational instruction.
